1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Driver of the csv-tools program: seed the git repository the program delivers
4	 * into with the specification, the command line and the committed test suite,
5	 * record the two signatures, run the three-department program to its release,
6	 * and print the ledger, the member sessions, the barrier refusals and the file
7	 * list of the merged tree.
8	 *
9	 * The same driver serves the keyless composition beside it and the Claude Code
10	 * overlay under `overlays/`: what changes between the two is the route the
11	 * departments are driven on, never the spec, so both runs carry one program id.
12	 */
13	
14	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
15	import { cpSync, existsSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
16	import { join } from 'node:path'
17	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
18	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
19	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
20	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
21	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
22	import { programIdFor, programSpecDigest, resolveProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
23	import type { ProgramReport, ProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
24	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
25	import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
26	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
27	import type { SessionPersistence } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
28	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff'
29	import type { CheckId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
30	
31	/** The artefact both of the program's signatures attest: the frozen specification. */
32	const ARTEFACT = 'c'.repeat(64)
33	
34	/** Caps every department session runs under. */
35	const BUDGET = { maxTotalTokens: 2_000_000, maxWallMs: 1_500_000 }
36	
37	/** The check every department carries: a department installs nothing. */
38	const NO_DEPENDENCIES = 'test ! -e node_modules'
39	
40	/** One program session's ledger as the e2e asserts on it. */
41	interface LedgerLine {
42	  readonly sessionId: string
43	  readonly events: { readonly type: string; readonly data: unknown }[]
44	  /** Transitions the same session was signed for, in log order. */
45	  readonly signoffs: string[]
46	}
47	
48	/** One recorded run of a member session's own standard. */
49	interface RunLine {
50	  readonly attempt: number
51	  readonly verdict: string
52	  readonly results: { readonly checkId: string; readonly status: string }[]
53	}
54	
55	/** One member session's stamp, caps, runs and certificate. */
56	interface MemberLine {
57	  readonly sessionId: string
58	  readonly programId: string
59	  readonly key: string
60	  readonly certified: boolean
61	  readonly caps: unknown
62	  readonly runs: RunLine[]
63	  /** Root causes the validator addressed to this session, in log order. */
64	  readonly directives: string[]
65	}
66	
67	/** One refusal the read barrier recorded. */
68	interface DenialLine {
69	  readonly sessionId: string
70	  readonly capability: string
71	  readonly displayPath: string
72	}
73	
74	const configPath = process.argv[2]
75	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('csv-tools driver requires a config path')
76	
77	const repository = process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO
78	if (repository === undefined) throw new Error('csv-tools driver requires DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO')
79	
80	// The roster's root has to be absolute and the smoke runs in an isolated
81	// temporary cwd, so the presets beside this file are exported by path.
82	process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_PRESETS = fileURLToPath(new URL('presets', import.meta.url))
83	
84	// A host that configures git through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` hands every child a
85	// command-line config the shell seam cannot forward whole, and git then refuses
86	// every invocation. This fixture runs against its own repository, so it drops
87	// the whole set rather than inheriting half of it.
88	for (const name of Object.keys(process.env)) {
89	  if (name.startsWith('GIT_CONFIG_')) Reflect.deleteProperty(process.env, name)
90	}
91	
92	/**
93	 * Create the repository the program delivers into, once: the specification, the
94	 * command line and the test suite of `seed/`, committed and tagged `base`.
95	 * @param root - where the repository is minted.
96	 */
97	function ensureRepository(root: string): void {
98	  if (existsSync(join(root, '.git'))) return
99	  mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true })
100	  cpSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('seed', import.meta.url)), root, { recursive: true })
101	  const git = (...args: string[]): void => void execFileSync('git', args, { cwd: root, stdio: 'pipe' })
102	  git('init', '-q', '.')
103	  git('config', 'user.email', 'csv-tools@example.test')
104	  git('config', 'user.name', 'csv-tools program')
105	  git('add', '-A')
106	  git('commit', '-qm', 'the csv-tools specification, command line and test suite')
107	  git('tag', 'base')
108	}
109	
110	/**
111	 * The program the fixture runs: the parser and `stats` first, then `filter` and
112	 * `join`, then one integration over the merged head.
113	 * @returns the spec, which is frozen and digested before anything runs.
114	 */
115	function programSpec(): ProgramSpec {
116	  const department = (key: string, files: string, delivers: string, suite: string): ProgramSpec['goals'][number] => ({
117	    key,
118	    objective: [
119	      `csv-tools department: ${key}.`,
120	      'Read `SPEC.md` at the root of this worktree first: it is the whole specification and the only one.',
121	      `Deliver ${files} — ${delivers} — exactly as \`SPEC.md\` states them, then commit.`,
122	      'Do not change `bin/csv-tools.js` or anything under `test/`, and install nothing.',
123	      `Your work is measured by \`${suite}\` over a clean worktree, so commit before you stop.`,
124	    ].join(' '),
125	    preset: 'implementing',
126	    isolation: 'none',
127	    budget: BUDGET,
128	    dependsOn: key === 'stats' ? [] : ['stats'],
129	    checks: [
130	      { id: `${key}-suite` as CheckId, outcome: `the committed suite for ${key} passes`, run: suite },
131	      { id: `${key}-no-dependencies` as CheckId, outcome: 'nothing was installed', run: NO_DEPENDENCIES },
132	    ],
133	  })
134	  return {
135	    objective: 'deliver csv-tools: a zero-dependency command line with stats, filter and join subcommands',
136	    baseRevision: 'base',
137	    signoff: { artefactSha256: ARTEFACT },
138	    goals: [
139	      department(
140	        'stats',
141	        '`src/csv.js` and `src/stats.js`',
142	        'the reader and writer every subcommand is built on, and the `stats` subcommand',
143	        'node --test test/csv.test.js test/stats.test.js',
144	      ),
145	      department('filter', '`src/filter.js`', 'the `filter` subcommand', 'node --test test/filter.test.js'),
146	      department('join', '`src/join.js`', 'the `join` subcommand', 'node --test test/join.test.js'),
147	    ],
148	    integration: {
149	      // Only the merged head carries all four modules, so only the merged head
150	      // passes `test/cli.test.js` — the suite that drives the real command line.
151	      checks: [{
152	        id: 'csv-tools-suite' as CheckId,
153	        outcome: 'the merged head passes every committed suite, including the command line end to end',
154	        run: 'node --test test/*.test.js',
155	      }],
156	      // The commit-or-refuse rule, carried into the certificate rather than
157	      // only into the program's own refusal to measure a dirty worktree.
158	      gates: ['test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"', NO_DEPENDENCIES],
159	    },
160	  }
161	}
162	
163	/**
164	 * Record the spec-freeze and release signatures on the program session, the way
165	 * a client district's signer would before the program starts. A session that
166	 * already carries them is left alone, so a resumed run signs nothing twice.
167	 * @param ctx - the booted application.
168	 * @param spec - the spec whose digest names the program session.
169	 * @param cwd - the repository the signing session is opened over.
170	 */
171	async function sign(ctx: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof boot>>, spec: ProgramSpec, cwd: string): Promise<void> {
172	  const sessionId = SessionId(programIdFor(programSpecDigest(resolveProgramSpec(spec))))
173	  const signoffs = ctx.get('signoffs')
174	  const agents = ctx.get('agents')
175	  if (signoffs === undefined || agents === undefined) throw new Error('csv-tools driver requires the signoffs and agents services')
176	  if ((await ctx.get('sessionPersistence')?.list() ?? []).some(stored => stored.id === sessionId)) return
177	  const model = ctx.get('agentDefaultModel')?.currentSelection()
178	  if (model === undefined) throw new Error('csv-tools driver requires the default-model service')
179	  const handle = await agents.create({
180	    sessionId,
181	    meta: { cwd },
182	    agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
183	  })
184	  try {
185	    for (const transition of ['spec-freeze', 'release'] as const) {
186	      signoffs.record(handle.agent, {
187	        transition,
188	        principal: { kind: 'human', id: 'csv-tools-client', displayName: 'csv-tools client' },
189	        artefactSha256: ARTEFACT,
190	        evidence: [{ kind: 'spec', ref: 'the frozen csv-tools program spec' }],
191	      })
192	    }
193	    await ctx.sessions.flush(handle.agent.session)
194	  } finally {
195	    await handle.dispose()
196	  }
197	}
198	
199	/**
200	 * Every program ledger and every member session in the persistence root.
201	 * @param persistence - the backend the composition mounted.
202	 * @returns the ledgers and the member lines the e2e asserts on.
203	 */
204	async function readRoot(persistence: SessionPersistence): Promise<{ ledgers: LedgerLine[]; members: MemberLine[] }> {
205	  const ledgers: LedgerLine[] = []
206	  const members: MemberLine[] = []
207	  for (const stored of await persistence.list()) {
208	    const { events } = await persistence.inspect(stored.id)
209	    const programEvents = events.filter((event: SessionEvent) => event.type.startsWith('program/') && event.type !== 'program/member')
210	    if (programEvents.length > 0) {
211	      ledgers.push({
212	        sessionId: stored.id,
213	        events: programEvents.map(event => ({ type: event.type, data: event.data })),
214	        signoffs: events.flatMap(event => (event.type === 'signoff/recorded' ? [event.data.transition] : [])),
215	      })
216	    }
217	    for (const event of events) {
218	      if (event.type !== 'program/member') continue
219	      members.push({
220	        sessionId: stored.id,
221	        programId: event.data.programId,
222	        key: event.data.key,
223	        certified: events.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'verification/certificate'),
224	        caps: events.find(candidate => candidate.type === 'budget/caps')?.data,
225	        runs: events.flatMap(candidate => (candidate.type === 'verification/run'
226	          ? [{
227	            attempt: candidate.data.attempt,
228	            verdict: candidate.data.verdict,
229	            results: candidate.data.results.map(result => ({ checkId: result.checkId as string, status: result.status })),
230	          }]
231	          : [])),
232	        directives: events.flatMap(candidate => (candidate.type === 'verification/directive' ? [candidate.data.rootCause] : [])),
233	      })
234	    }
235	  }
236	  return { ledgers, members }
237	}
238	
239	/**
240	 * The files the released tree carries.
241	 * @param root - the repository the program delivered into.
242	 * @param report - the report whose merged revision is read.
243	 * @returns every path of the merged tree, sorted, or an empty list for a program that released none.
244	 */
245	function deliverable(root: string, report: ProgramReport): string[] {
246	  if (report.mergedRevision === undefined) return []
247	  const listed = execFileSync('git', ['ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', report.mergedRevision], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' })
248	  return listed.split('\n').filter(line => line !== '').sort()
249	}
250	
251	// The repository has to exist before the program plugin validates its
252	// workspaceRoot, so it is minted before the composition loads.
253	ensureRepository(repository)
254	
255	const ctx = await boot('csv-tools-program', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
256	try {
257	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the program mounts presets and reads
258	  // persisted sessions, so the driver drives only the settled application.
259	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
260	  const programs = ctx.get('programs')
261	  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
262	  if (programs === undefined || persistence === undefined) throw new Error('csv-tools driver requires the programs and session persistence services')
263	  const denials: DenialLine[] = []
264	  ctx.on('session/event', (session, event) => {
265	    if (event.type === 'read-barrier/denied') {
266	      denials.push({ sessionId: session.id, capability: event.data.capability, displayPath: event.data.displayPath })
267	    }
268	  }, { global: true })
269	  const spec = programSpec()
270	  await sign(ctx, spec, repository)
271	  const report = await programs.start(spec)
272	  const observed = await readRoot(persistence)
273	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({
274	    type: 'result',
275	    report,
276	    denials,
277	    deliverable: deliverable(repository, report),
278	    ...observed,
279	  })}\n`)
280	} finally {
281	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
282	}
283

2	# command line — three departments, one git worktree and session each, an
3	# integration over the merged head, and a ledger in the program's own session.
4	#
5	# This file is the keyless half: the departments run on the scripted `cli-mock`
6	# route below, so the whole workflow executes with no key and no product
7	# installation. `overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml` is the same composition with
8	# the operator's Claude Code route in its place, which is the one the real run
9	# boots; nothing else differs between the two.
10	- id: csv-tools-llm
11	  name: './csv-tools-llm.ts'
12	
13	# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor (spawn/kill/output plumbing).
14	- id: subprocess
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'
16	
17	- id: bash
18	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'
19	
20	- id: fs
21	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'
22	  config:
23	    cwd: !!js process.cwd()
24	
25	# The barrier the program denies its integration session the department
26	# worktrees with; the fs gate is what refuses the read in the operation that
27	# opens paths. The self-assessment run of 2026-09-08 had no barrier, and its
28	# unconfined integration session edited a department's certified file.
29	- id: read-barrier
30	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
31	
32	- id: fs-read-barrier
33	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier'
34	
35	- id: tool-fs
36	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
37	
38	- id: goal
39	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
40	  config:
41	    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 11
42	
43	# Composed beside the program, which disarms every goal it creates: a department
44	# an operator resumes by hand is driven by this row instead.
45	- id: goal-round-driver
46	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver'
47	
48	- id: verification
49	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
50	  config:
51	    maxChecks: 32
52	    maxTextChars: 2048
53	
54	# The roster's root is absolute: the smoke runs in an isolated temporary cwd, so
55	# the presets beside this file are reachable only through the path the driver exports.
56	- id: agent-presets
57	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
58	  config:
59	    default: implementing
60	    roots:
61	      - path: !!js process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_PRESETS
62	        trust: system
63	    includeUserRoot: false

1	/**
2	 * Keyless adapter that plays every department of the csv-tools program: read
3	 * the specification, write the modules that department owns, commit them.
4	 *
5	 * The bodies it writes are the committed files under `scripted/src/`, so what
6	 * the department delivers is reviewable source rather than a string assembled
7	 * here, and the session transcript carries the same bytes the branch does. The
8	 * `join` department deliberately stops before committing on its first attempt:
9	 * the program refuses to measure a worktree carrying work no commit carries,
10	 * and the turn that follows its `<uncommitted_work>` directive commits.
11	 *
12	 * The markers and the department keys below are pinned by the e2e and by the
13	 * driver's spec, so keep them and the goal objectives together.
14	 */
15	
16	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
17	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
18	import {
19	  CallId,
20	  LlmAdapter,
21	  type GenerateOptions,
22	  type LlmResolvedModelInfo,
23	  type StreamChunk,
24	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
25	
26	/** The turn text the program delivers when a worktree carries uncommitted work. */
27	const UNCOMMITTED_MARKER = '<uncommitted_work>'
28	
29	/** The turn text the program delivers when a standard did not pass. */
30	const CHECKS_FAILED_MARKER = '<checks_failed>'
31	
32	/** The specification every department reads before it writes anything. */
33	const SPEC = 'SPEC.md'
34	
35	/** The answer that ends a department's turn. */
36	const DONE = 'TURN COMPLETE'
37	
38	/** What each department's goal objective states, and what it delivers. */
39	const DEPARTMENT_FILES: Record<string, readonly string[]> = {
40	  stats: ['src/csv.js', 'src/stats.js'],
41	  filter: ['src/filter.js'],
42	  join: ['src/join.js'],
43	}
44	
45	/** The department that leaves its first attempt uncommitted. */
46	const UNCOMMITTED_DEPARTMENT = 'join'
47	
48	/** Scripted body per worktree path, read once from the files committed beside this plugin. */
49	const SOURCES: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map(
50	  Object.values(DEPARTMENT_FILES).flat().map(path => [
51	    path,
52	    readFileSync(new URL(`scripted/${path}`, import.meta.url), 'utf8'),
53	  ]),
54	)
55	
56	/** Where in one session's turn the adapter is: the turn's text and the tool results it already has. */
57	interface Position {
58	  /** Text of the newest turn the session was handed, empty for a session that was handed none. */
59	  readonly text: string
60	  /** Tool results delivered since that turn, which is the step this stream serves. */
61	  readonly results: number
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Read the newest turn and the steps already taken in it.
66	 * @param options - the request the loop assembled.
67	 * @returns the turn text and the tool results that followed it.
68	 */
69	function position(options: GenerateOptions): Position {
70	  let results = 0
71	  for (let index = options.messages.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
72	    const message = options.messages[index]
73	    if (message === undefined || message.role !== 'user') continue
74	    const content = message.content ?? []
75	    if (content.some(block => block.type === 'tool-result')) {
76	      results += 1
77	      continue
78	    }
79	    return { text: content.filter(block => block.type === 'text').map(block => block.text).join(''), results }
80	  }
81	  return { text: '', results }
82	}
83	
84	/**
85	 * The department this session works, from the marker its goal objective carries.
86	 * @param options - the request whose history carries the goal text.
87	 * @returns the key, or `undefined` for a session that was never given one.
88	 */
89	function departmentKey(options: GenerateOptions): string | undefined {
90	  const history = options.messages
91	    .flatMap(message => message.content ?? [])
92	    .flatMap(block => (block.type === 'text' ? [block.text] : []))
93	    .join('\n')
94	  const key = /csv-tools department: ([a-z-]+)/.exec(history)?.[1]
95	  return key !== undefined && Object.hasOwn(DEPARTMENT_FILES, key) ? key : undefined
96	}
97	
98	/**
99	 * The commit one department makes once its files are written.
100	 * @param key - the department's goal key.
101	 * @returns the arguments of the `bash` call that commits them.
102	 */
103	function commitCall(key: string): object {
104	  return {
105	    command: `git add -A && git commit -qm 'deliver the ${key} part of csv-tools'`,
106	    description: 'Commit what this department delivers.',
107	  }
108	}
109	
110	class CsvToolsAdapter extends LlmAdapter {
111	  override async resolveModel(provider: string, model: string): Promise<LlmResolvedModelInfo> {
112	    return { provider, id: model, name: model }
113	  }
114	
115	  async * stream(options: GenerateOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
116	    const { text, results } = position(options)
117	    const key = departmentKey(options)
118	    if (key === undefined) {
119	      // The integration session and anything else this route is asked for: the
120	      // scripted implementer answers for departments only, so a turn here means
121	      // the merged head failed its own standard and the program must say so.
122	      yield * reply(`NO CSV-TOOLS DEPARTMENT IN THIS SESSION${text.includes(CHECKS_FAILED_MARKER) ? ': the merged head did not pass' : ''}`)
123	      return
124	    }
125	    if (text.includes(UNCOMMITTED_MARKER)) {
126	      if (results === 0) {
127	        yield * call('commit-after-directive', 'bash', commitCall(key))
128	        return
129	      }
130	      yield * reply(DONE)
131	      return
132	    }
133	    const files = DEPARTMENT_FILES[key] ?? []
134	    if (results === 0) {
135	      yield * call('read-spec', 'read', { file_path: SPEC })
136	      return
137	    }
138	    const pending = files[results - 1]
139	    if (pending !== undefined) {
140	      yield * call(`write-${pending.replaceAll('/', '-')}`, 'write', { file_path: pending, content: SOURCES.get(pending) })
141	      return
142	    }
143	    if (results === files.length + 1 && key !== UNCOMMITTED_DEPARTMENT) {
144	      yield * call('commit', 'bash', commitCall(key))
145	      return
146	    }
147	    yield * reply(DONE)
148	  }
149	}
150	
151	/**
152	 * One tool call as the canonical block sequence of a step that stops on tool calls.
153	 * @param id - the call's id, which the e2e and the transcript read.
154	 * @param name - the tool to call.
155	 * @param args - the call's arguments.
156	 * @yields the block sequence of one tool-calling step.
157	 */
158	function * call(id: string, name: string, args: object): Generator<StreamChunk> {
159	  const serialized = JSON.stringify(args)
160	  yield { type: 'block-start', index: 0, blockType: 'tool-call' }
161	  yield { type: 'tool-call-delta', index: 0, id: CallId(id), name, argumentsDelta: serialized }
162	  yield { type: 'block-end', index: 0, block: { type: 'tool-call', id: CallId(id), name, arguments: serialized } }
163	  yield { type: 'usage', usage: { inputTokens: 23, outputTokens: 7 } }
164	  yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'tool-calls' } }
165	}
166	
167	/**
168	 * One text answer as the canonical block sequence of a stopped step.
169	 * @param text - what the step answers.
170	 * @yields the block sequence of one stopped step.
171	 */
172	function * reply(text: string): Generator<StreamChunk> {
173	  yield { type: 'block-start', index: 0, blockType: 'text' }
174	  yield { type: 'text-delta', index: 0, text }
175	  yield { type: 'block-end', index: 0, block: { type: 'text', text } }
176	  yield { type: 'usage', usage: { inputTokens: 19, outputTokens: 3 } }
177	  yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'stop' } }
178	}
179	
180	export const name = 'csv-tools-llm'
181	
182	export const inject = ['llm']
183	
184	/**
185	 * Register the keyless `cli-mock` adapter this composition's departments run on.
186	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the LLM runtime.
187	 */
188	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
189	  ctx.llm.registerAdapter(['cli-mock'], new CsvToolsAdapter())
190	}

=== overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml ===
# The csv-tools program with the operator's own Claude Code installation as the
# route every department is driven through: the real run, and the only file that
# differs from the keyless composition beside it.
#
# `implementer` stays `route`, so the program drives each department turn by
# turn through the LLM seam and the department's own session holds every step it
# took. The spec digest covers the implementer but not the route, so the keyless
# and the real run are the same program id over the same goals.
- id: base
  name: '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include'
  config:
    path: ../cordis.yml
    patches:
      # The scripted adapter is the keyless half's whole reason to exist; a real
      # run composes no mock route at all.
      - id: csv-tools-llm
        disabled: true
      - insert:
          - id: llm-claude-code
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
            config:
              provider: claude-code
              models:
                - id: sonnet
                  name: Claude Code sonnet
                  productModel: sonnet
                  contextWindow: 200000
                - id: opus
                  name: Claude Code opus
                  productModel: opus
                  contextWindow: 200000
              effort: high
      - id: agent-default-model
        config:
          provider: claude-code
          model: opus

=== presets/implementing/agent.cordis.yml ===
# Every department of this program builds one part of the same command line, so
# all three mount this one preset: the deployment's bash and filesystem tools
# are what a department inherits, and the declared implementer role forbids any
# tool that carries an authority.

1	/**
2	 * Keyless REAL-composition coverage for a program that builds software: one
3	 * boot of `fixtures/program-csv-tools/cordis.yml` over a temporary git
4	 * repository seeded with the csv-tools specification, command line and test
5	 * suite. Three departments deliver the reader, `stats`, `filter` and `join` on
6	 * their own branches; the integration merges them and certifies the merged head
7	 * against the committed suite.
8	 *
9	 * The scripted implementer writes the modules committed under the fixture's
10	 * `scripted/`, so what this proves is the wiring — the spec freezes, the
11	 * departments are staffed and certified over committed trees, the branches
12	 * merge, and the committed verifier decides the release — not what a model can
13	 * build. The overlay under the fixture's `overlays/` is the same program driven
14	 * on the operator's Claude Code route, which is what answers that question.
15	 */
16	
17	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
18	import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
19	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
20	import { join } from 'node:path'
21	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
22	import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
23	import { LOADER_SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS, runLoaderSmoke } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke'
24	import { INTEGRATION_KEY } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
25	import type { ProgramEnd, ProgramGoalRecord, ProgramIntegrationRecord, ProgramStart } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
26	
27	const fixtureDir = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixtures/program-csv-tools/', import.meta.url))
28	const binScript = join(fixtureDir, 'driver.ts')
29	const configPath = join(fixtureDir, 'cordis.yml')
30	const repoTsconfig = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../tsconfig.json', import.meta.url))
31	
32	/** Three departments, an integration and a full node:test suite outrun the default window. */
33	const PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000
34	
35	/** Every path the released tree carries, which is the seed plus the four delivered modules. */
36	const DELIVERABLE = [
37	  'SPEC.md',
38	  'bin/csv-tools.js',
39	  'package.json',
40	  'src/csv.js',
41	  'src/filter.js',
42	  'src/join.js',
43	  'src/stats.js',
44	  'test/cli.test.js',
45	  'test/csv.test.js',
46	  'test/filter.test.js',
47	  'test/join.test.js',
48	  'test/stats.test.js',
49	]
50	
51	/** Seed files no department may change, checked byte for byte against the merged tree. */
52	const IMMUTABLE = ['SPEC.md', 'bin/csv-tools.js', 'test/cli.test.js']
53	
54	interface RunLine {
55	  attempt: number
56	  verdict: string
57	  results: { checkId: string; status: string }[]
58	}
59	
60	interface MemberLine {
61	  sessionId: string
62	  programId: string
63	  key: string
64	  certified: boolean
65	  caps: unknown
66	  runs: RunLine[]
67	  directives: string[]
68	}
69	
70	interface DriverResult {
71	  type: string
72	  report: {
73	    programId: string
74	    sessionId: string
75	    outcome?: string
76	    mergedRevision?: string
77	    goals: { key: string; status: string; revision?: string; tree?: string }[]
78	  }
79	  ledgers: { sessionId: string; events: { type: string; data: unknown }[]; signoffs: string[] }[]
80	  members: MemberLine[]
81	  denials: { sessionId: string; capability: string; displayPath: string }[]
82	  deliverable: string[]
83	}
84	
85	const roots: string[] = []
86	
87	afterAll(async () => {
88	  await Promise.all(roots.splice(0).map(root => rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })))
89	})
90	
91	/** The statuses one ledger recorded for one goal key, in log order. */
92	function statuses(events: { type: string; data: unknown }[], key: string): string[] {
93	  return events
94	    .filter(event => event.type === 'program/goal' && (event.data as ProgramGoalRecord).key === key)
95	    .map(event => (event.data as ProgramGoalRecord).status)
96	}
97	
98	/** The member line of one goal key, which every key of a released program has. */
99	function memberOf(observed: DriverResult, key: string): MemberLine {
100	  const found = observed.members.find(member => member.programId === observed.report.programId && member.key === key)
101	  expect(found, `no member session for ${key}`).toBeDefined()
102	  return found as MemberLine
103	}
104	
105	describe('a program that builds csv-tools through a real cordis.yml', () => {
106	  it('certifies three departments over committed trees and releases the merged command line', async () => {
107	    const sessions = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'csv-tools-sessions-'))
108	    const repository = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'csv-tools-repo-'))
109	    roots.push(sessions, repository)
110	
111	    const { stdout, stderr } = await runLoaderSmoke({
112	      label: 'program-csv-tools',
113	      tempDirPrefix: 'program-csv-tools-e2e-',
114	      binScript,
115	      libBinScript: binScript,
116	      configPath,
117	      binArgs: [configPath],
118	      tsconfigPath: repoTsconfig,
119	      processTimeoutMs: PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS,
120	      env: { DSH_TEST_SESSION_ROOT: sessions, DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO: repository },
121	    })
122	    expect(stderr).toBe('')
123	    const observed = JSON.parse(stdout.trimEnd().split('\n').at(-1) ?? '') as DriverResult
124	    expect(observed.type).toBe('result')
125	
126	    expect(observed.report.outcome).toBe('released')
127	    expect(observed.report.goals.map(goal => [goal.key, goal.status]))
128	      .toEqual([['stats', 'merged'], ['filter', 'merged'], ['join', 'merged']])
129	
130	    const ledger = observed.ledgers.find(candidate => candidate.sessionId === observed.report.programId)
131	    expect(ledger, 'no ledger for the program').toBeDefined()
132	    const events = ledger?.events ?? []
133	    const opened = events[0]?.data as ProgramStart
134	    expect(events[0]?.type).toBe('program/start')
135	    expect(opened.specSha256).toBe(observed.report.programId.replace('program-', ''))
136	    expect(opened.baseRevision).toBe('base')
137	    // The spec is frozen before anything runs, and the route the departments are
138	    // driven on is not part of it: the overlay's real run is this same program.
139	    expect(opened.implementer).toEqual({ kind: 'route' })
140	    expect(ledger?.signoffs).toEqual(['spec-freeze', 'release'])
141	
142	    // `filter` and `join` depend on the department that owns the reader, so
143	    // neither starts before that one holds a certificate.
144	    expect(statuses(events, 'stats')).toEqual(['pending', 'running', 'certified', 'merged'])
145	    expect(statuses(events, 'filter')).toEqual(['pending', 'running', 'certified', 'merged'])
146	    expect(statuses(events, 'join')).toEqual(['pending', 'running', 'certified', 'merged'])
147	    const integrations = events
148	      .filter(event => event.type === 'program/integration')
149	      .map(event => event.data as ProgramIntegrationRecord)
150	    expect(integrations.map(record => record.status)).toEqual(['running', 'certified'])
151	    const closing = events.at(-1)?.data as ProgramEnd
152	    expect(events.at(-1)?.type).toBe('program/end')
153	    expect(closing.outcome).toBe('released')
154	
155	    // Every department was certified over a commit of its own, and the ledger
156	    // records both the revision and the tree that certificate covers.
157	    const certified = observed.report.goals.map(goal => goal.revision)
158	    expect(certified.every(revision => /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(revision ?? ''))).toBe(true)
159	    expect(new Set(certified).size).toBe(3)
160	    expect(observed.report.goals.every(goal => /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(goal.tree ?? ''))).toBe(true)
161	    expect(certified).not.toContain(observed.report.mergedRevision)
162	
163	    // The `join` department leaves its first attempt uncommitted: the program
164	    // refuses to measure that worktree, names why, and certifies the attempt
165	    // that commits.
166	    const joinDepartment = memberOf(observed, 'join')
167	    expect(joinDepartment.directives).toEqual(['the worktree carries work that no commit on this branch carries'])
168	    expect(joinDepartment.runs.map(run => run.verdict)).toEqual(['passed'])
169	    expect(joinDepartment.certified).toBe(true)
170	
171	    // Each department runs under the caps the spec gave it and is certified on
172	    // exactly two checks: its own part of the committed suite, and the rule that
173	    // it installed nothing.
174	    for (const key of ['stats', 'filter', 'join']) {
175	      const department = memberOf(observed, key)
176	      expect(department.caps).toEqual({ maxTotalTokens: 2_000_000, maxWallMs: 1_500_000 })
177	      expect(department.runs.at(-1)?.results.map(result => [result.checkId, result.status]))
178	        .toEqual([[`${key}-suite`, 'pass'], [`${key}-no-dependencies`, 'pass']])
179	    }
180	    expect(observed.members.filter(member => member.programId === observed.report.programId).map(member => member.key).sort())
181	      .toEqual(['@integration', 'filter', 'join', 'stats'])
182	
183	    // The committed verifier is what releases the program: the whole suite,
184	    // including the command line no department branch can satisfy, plus the two
185	    // gates the certificate carries.
186	    const integration = memberOf(observed, INTEGRATION_KEY)
187	    expect(integration.runs).toHaveLength(1)
188	    expect(integration.runs[0]?.results.map(result => [result.checkId, result.status]))
189	      .toEqual([['csv-tools-suite', 'pass'], ['gate-1', 'pass'], ['gate-2', 'pass']])
190	    // The merged head passed on the merge alone, so the integration session was
191	    // never given a turn and refused no read; the denial it ran under is still
192	    // recorded on the closing record.
193	    expect(observed.denials).toEqual([])
194	    expect(integrations.at(-1)?.denied).toEqual([join(repository, observed.report.programId)])
195	
196	    // The released tree is the seed plus exactly the four modules the three
197	    // departments own, with every file the spec froze unchanged.
198	    expect(observed.deliverable).toEqual(DELIVERABLE)
199	    for (const path of IMMUTABLE) {
200	      const merged = execFileSync('git', ['show', `${observed.report.mergedRevision}:${path}`], { cwd: repository, encoding: 'utf8' })
201	      expect(merged).toBe(await readFile(join(fixtureDir, 'seed', path), 'utf8'))
202	    }
203	
204	    // The command line the program delivered runs: one subcommand from each
205	    // department, from the integration worktree the release was certified on.
206	    const samples = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'csv-tools-samples-'))
207	    roots.push(samples)
208	    const people = join(samples, 'people.csv')

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	// Mechanical verifier for assessment.md: structure, verdict lines, citations
3	// that resolve to files under evidence/, and bounds. Exit 0 when every rule
4	// holds; otherwise print each failure and exit 1.
5	import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
6	import { join, dirname } from 'node:path'
7	
8	const path = process.argv[2] ?? 'assessment.md'
9	const failures = []
10	if (!existsSync(path)) {
11	  console.error(`missing ${path}`)
12	  process.exit(1)
13	}
14	const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8')
15	const root = dirname(path) === '.' ? process.cwd() : dirname(path)
16	const sections = ['## Verdict', '## Evidence', '## What the evidence does not support', '## What would change the verdict']
17	const positions = sections.map(s => text.indexOf(`\n${s}\n`) === -1 && !text.startsWith(`${s}\n`) ? -1 : (text.startsWith(`${s}\n`) ? 0 : text.indexOf(`\n${s}\n`)))
18	sections.forEach((s, i) => { if (positions[i] === -1) failures.push(`section missing: ${s}`) })
19	for (let i = 1; i < positions.length; i++) {
20	  if (positions[i] !== -1 && positions[i - 1] !== -1 && positions[i] < positions[i - 1]) failures.push(`section out of order: ${sections[i]}`)
21	}
22	const body = (name) => {
23	  const i = sections.indexOf(name)
24	  if (positions[i] === -1) return ''
25	  const start = positions[i] + name.length + 1
26	  const next = positions.slice(i + 1).filter(p => p !== -1).sort((a, b) => a - b)[0]
27	  return text.slice(start, next === undefined ? text.length : next)
28	}
29	const verdict = body('## Verdict')
30	if (!/^Viable: (yes|no|undetermined) \((high|medium|low) confidence\)/m.test(verdict)) failures.push('verdict line missing: "Viable: yes|no|undetermined (high|medium|low confidence)"')
31	if (!/^State of the art: (yes|no|in part|undetermined) \((high|medium|low) confidence\)/m.test(verdict)) failures.push('verdict line missing: "State of the art: yes|no|in part|undetermined (high|medium|low confidence)"')
32	const bullets = (s) => s.split('\n').filter(l => /^\s*[-*] /.test(l))
33	const evidenceBullets = bullets(body('## Evidence'))
34	if (evidenceBullets.length < 8) failures.push(`evidence needs at least 8 bullets, found ${evidenceBullets.length}`)
35	const cited = new Set()
36	for (const line of evidenceBullets) {
37	  const refs = [...line.matchAll(/evidence\/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/g)].map(m => m[1])
38	  if (refs.length === 0) failures.push(`evidence bullet without a citation: ${line.trim().slice(0, 80)}`)
39	  for (const ref of refs) {
40	    if (!existsSync(join(root, 'evidence', ref))) failures.push(`citation does not resolve: evidence/${ref}`)
41	    else cited.add(ref)
42	  }
43	}
44	if (cited.size < 6) failures.push(`at least 6 distinct evidence files must be cited, found ${cited.size}`)
45	if (bullets(body('## What the evidence does not support')).length < 3) failures.push('"What the evidence does not support" needs at least 3 bullets')
46	if (bullets(body('## What would change the verdict')).length < 3) failures.push('"What would change the verdict" needs at least 3 bullets')
47	const words = text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length
48	if (words < 600 || words > 2500) failures.push(`length must be 600 to 2500 words, found ${words}`)
49	if (/TODO|TBD|lorem/i.test(text)) failures.push('placeholder text present')
50	if (failures.length > 0) {
51	  for (const f of failures) console.error(`FAIL ${f}`)
52	  process.exit(1)
53	}
54	console.log(`ok: ${evidenceBullets.length} evidence bullets, ${cited.size} files cited, ${words} words`)

# The question, the goals, and the rules of this assessment

You are assessing an open-source project, DeepSeek Harness as built by the Daliesk lab, from the evidence in this directory only. The evidence is the project's own records: run records and their README, Agent Notes, a census of what cells reached outside their workspace, the commit log of the last thirty hours, and a comparison with two external systems. Some files are the project's own summaries of itself (`results-draft.md`, `roles-matrix.md`); prefer the primary records (`proving-ground-README.md`, `census.txt`, `records-index.txt`, `commits-last-30h.txt`) whenever a summary and a record could disagree.

## The project's stated goals

1. The best harness: a plugin-based agent harness that makes any LLM the best agentic coder it can be.
2. The best agentic software creation through that harness.
3. A roughly 120B-parameter open-weight model trained with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards on the harness's certified runs.
4. A loop in which the harness improves itself: frozen paired experiments whose verdicts promote or reject changes.

## The two questions

- **Viable**: given the evidence, can this project reach its stated goals with the means the evidence shows (one operator's subscription, agents as the workforce, the bench and district as instruments)? Answer `yes`, `no`, or `undetermined`, with a confidence.
- **State of the art**: given the evidence, is any part of this project ahead of the field the evidence describes (the competitive baselines, the ruflo comparison, the hypothesis slate's summary of the quarter's results)? Answer `yes`, `no`, `in part`, or `undetermined`, with a confidence, and name the part.

## Rules

- Every claim in the evidence section cites the file it comes from, as `(evidence/<file>)`. A claim without a citation is not evidence.
- Distinguish what was measured from what was built, and what was built from what was planned.
- A refutation counts as much as a confirmation. An inconclusive verdict is reported as inconclusive, never rounded toward either side.
- Where the project's own summary makes a claim the records do not carry, say so.
- Write for a reader who will act on the verdict: name what would change it.

3	 * the seven `program/*` events its sessions carry, and the reconciled state a

15	/** Identifies one program across every session and worktree it owns. */

18	/**

20	 * `budget/caps`. The three fields are the caps a program can state about a
21	 * department: token and wall-clock spend bound every deployment, and cost binds
22	 * one whose routes the budget policy prices.
23	 */

25	  /** Input plus output tokens the department's session may spend. */
26	  readonly maxTotalTokens?: number
27	  /** Milliseconds the department's session log may span. */
28	  readonly maxWallMs?: number
29	  /** EUR the department's priced routes may cost. */
30	  readonly maxCostEur?: number
31	}
32	
33	/** One goal of a program: what one department delivers, and what certifies it. */
34	export interface ProgramGoalSpec {
35	  /** Lower-kebab-case identity, unique in the program; it names the branch and the worktree. */
36	  readonly key: string
37	  /** The objective the department's goal is created with. */
38	  readonly objective: string
39	  /** Id of a shipped preset declaring the `implementer` role, mounted into the department session. */
40	  readonly preset: string
41	  /** Isolation the department's certified run claims. */
42	  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
43	  /** Caps recorded on the department session before its first turn. */
44	  readonly budget: ProgramGoalBudget
45	  /** Keys of the goals this one is delivered after; a directed acyclic graph over the program's keys. */
46	  readonly dependsOn: readonly string[]
47	  /** The standard the department is certified against, compiled before any department starts. */
48	  readonly checks: readonly StandardCheck[]
49	}
50	
51	/** What the merged head must satisfy before the program releases. */
52	export interface ProgramIntegrationSpec {
53	  /** The standard authored for the integration session over the merged head. */
54	  readonly checks: readonly StandardCheck[]
55	  /**
56	   * Shell commands the merged head must exit zero on, run in the integration
57	   * worktree beside the standard. Each becomes one `gate-<n>` check of the
58	   * integration standard, in this order, so the integration certificate covers
59	   * the gates as well as the checks.
60	   */
61	  readonly gates: readonly string[]

# dsh-agent-presets

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Per-preset agent composition. A **preset** is a directory holding one `agent.cordis.yml`; the roster mounts it ONCE per process under a standing scope, and each session that names it joins by having its agent scope key parented to the mount's (`dsh-scope`'s parent chain). The mount's tools, prompt sections, and projection units exist exactly once and cover every joined agent — its plugins key their state by Session/Agent, so sessions stay apart inside one shared instance — and a host reader with no agent at all (a cold transcript read) resolves the same standing registrations by preset id.

The mechanism is two seams. Entry contexts chain to the context a subtree was plugged into, and both [`dsh-tools`](../../core/tools/README.md) and [`dsh-system-prompt`](../../core/system-prompt/README.md) file registrations into the calling context's scope layer — so the standing mount's contributions land in the PRESET's layer. What carries them to each session is `dsh-scope`'s parent chain: an agent's views resolve `agent → preset → global` (nearest shadowing farthest), and the mount's listeners are admitted for every agent parented under it while a sibling preset's stay deaf.

## Service: `AgentPresets` (ctx key: `agentPresets`)

Discovery is unmemoized: `list()` and `resolve()` re-read the roots on every call, so a preset authored while the process runs is visible immediately and a deleted one disappears from the next read. Discovery also owns preset **health**: a directory whose composition is missing or unloadable (unparsable YAML — checked with the loader's own dialect, `!!js` included — or not a list of named plugin rows) is listed with a `broken` reason rather than skipped, because a skipped directory would still occupy its id on disk while every surface shows nothing to delete. A directory whose name is not a usable preset id (`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`) is skipped outright: no copy could ever claim it.

- `ctx.agentPresets.defaultId: string` The preset id mounted when a caller names none.
- `ctx.agentPresets.list(): Promise<AgentPreset[]>` Every preset the configured roots currently supply, earlier root winning a duplicate id; broken presets included, each carrying its reason.
- `ctx.agentPresets.resolve(id?): Promise<AgentPreset>` One preset by id, defaulting to `defaultId`. Throws naming the available ids when no root supplies it. A broken preset resolves — deleting, reading, and reporting one all need the row.
- `ctx.agentPresets.mount(agentCtx, id?): Promise<AgentPreset>` Compose one agent from a preset — ensure its standing mount (single-flight) and parent the agent's scope key to it — returning the preset for the caller to record. Refuses a broken preset up front with its discovery-reported reason, so every unloadable shape fails the same way before the loader is involved.
- `ctx.agentPresets.composeFrom(agentCtx, parentCtx): string | undefined` Join one agent to the standing composition another already runs on, returning the preset id joined — `undefined` when the parent joined none, which is the rosterless deployment and not an error. A bind rather than a mount, so it is synchronous and has no composition failure mode; it still rejects a caller error (an unscoped context, or an agent that already joined).
- `ctx.agentPresets.composedPreset(agentCtx): string | undefined` The preset one LIVE agent runs on, read from its scope chain rather than from its session — the only answer available for an agent whose durable header is still being built.
- `ctx.agentPresets.recompose(agentCtx, id): Promise<AgentPreset>` Re-link one agent to a different preset's standing composition. Valid only while the agent has produced nothing — **the caller owns that check**; the new mount is ensured before the link moves, so a failure leaves the agent as it was. Refuses a broken preset like `mount()`.
- `ctx.agentPresets.standingKeyFor(id?): Promise<ScopeKey>` The standing scope key a host reader with no agent (a cold transcript read) resolves preset registrations in; ensures the mount without starting an agent, session, or turn. Refuses a broken preset like `mount()`.
- `ctx.agentPresets.roots: readonly PresetRoot[]` The roots this roster scans — every configured root in order, then the derived harness-home root. Not `config.roots`: read this to answer whether a roster is composed at all, so one derivation decides it.
- `ctx.agentPresets.authorable: boolean` Whether any of those roots has `user` trust, and therefore whether a preset can be created at all.
- `ctx.agentPresets.read(id): Promise<string>` One preset's composition text, exactly as stored.
- `ctx.agentPresets.copy(from, id, name?): Promise<void>` Create a locally authored preset by copying an existing one's whole directory — the only authoring write. No composition text crosses this seam, so a copy is exactly as loadable as its source; the copied metadata keeps the source's description but never its name or roster order, and `name` (or the id fallback) is what distinguishes the rows.
- `ctx.agentPresets.remove(id): Promise<void>` Delete a locally authored preset; joined sessions keep their standing mount. Clears the user default when it named the preset just deleted: storing a default that does not exist yet is deliberate, but one this call removed will never be supplied again and would fail every session created without an explicit pick.

`AgentPreset` carries `id` (the directory name), `trust` (`system` or `user`, from the root it was found under), `path` (the absolute composition file), and — only when the preset cannot compose a session — `broken` (one human-readable reason, shown verbatim on roster surfaces).

### Where to call `mount()`

The agent factory's `setup(agentCtx)` hook is the one supported call site. Only there is the join installed while the agent is still unpublished, so a rejected composition rolls the whole creation back rather than leaving a half-composed session. The standing subtree is owned by the roster service's own fiber — deliberately its UNTRACED context, because a subtree minted from a traced `this.ctx` resolves every service through the caller's shadow fiber instead of each entry's own inject store — so it survives every agent and unwinds only with the whole tree. Each generation records its composition file's stamp (mtime and size): a session that finds the stamp stale starts the next generation, while every session already joined keeps the one it runs on — the composition a running session joined outlives its file changing or disappearing underneath it, and files are the only composition editor, so the stamp is what carries an edit to later sessions.

### Composing a child agent

A subagent's child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, never through `mount()`. Every model-facing row lives on the agent plane, so the tool registry's global layer is empty and a child that joins nothing reaches the model with no tools at all and none of its parent's prompt sections.

Re-mounting the parent's preset by id would differ from the bind in two ways that both matter. A composition file edited since the parent started would hand the child a DIFFERENT generation than the one its parent's history was produced under, and a preset deleted since would fail the child outright while its parent keeps running. The bind is also synchronous, which is what lets the in-process subagent drivers use it at all — they compose their children inside a synchronous creation window.

The child records the joined id on its own durable header ([`dsh-subagent`](../../subagent/subagent/README.md)), so a cold read of the child's history rebuilds the composition it actually ran under rather than the deployment default.

### Which preset a session runs

The creation header names the preset a session STARTED with; `resolveSessionPreset(session)` names the one it RUNS. They differ whenever a blank session switched, so every reconstruction path — the summary a picker reads, a resume, a fork — resolves rather than reading the header.

The header stays frozen because it is a creation fact. A switch is an `agent-preset/selected` session event appended after the swap commits, which is what the model-visible ⟺ logged rule requires: the preset decides the tool schemas and prompt sections the model sees, so it has to be reconstructable from the log. The service re-emits that committed fact as the non-scoped cordis event `agent-preset/selected(sessionId, agentPreset)` declared by the client-safe `./types` export, allowing remote consumers to invalidate session-derived state without importing Host runtime types. Reading the header alone would rebuild a switched session under the composition it was created with, replaying history the new tool set cannot act on — the exact hazard the blank-only lock exists to prevent.

### Switching a blank agent

`recompose()` unmounts the installed subtree and mounts the new one, because two compositions cannot coexist — both would register the same tool names into one layer. A failed mount restores the previous composition rather than leaving the agent with nothing, and an unknown id is rejected before anything is torn down.

The restriction to a produced-nothing agent is a product rule, not a mechanical one: swapping tools mid-conversation would leave logged tool calls the new composition cannot make. The gateway enforces it at the wire ([`dsh-apiproxy`](../../host/apiproxy/README.md) answers `agent-preset-locked`), which is where session history is in hand.

## Authoring

Authoring is copy-only. A new preset is a whole-directory copy of an existing one — composition, metadata, skill directories, assets — landed under the first `user` root; the inputs are two ids the service resolves against its own roots plus an optional display name, so no caller ever supplies composition text and a copy grants nothing the roster did not already carry. Everything after creation happens in the preset's own files. `copy()` refuses three things before anything lands:

- **An id that is not `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`.** The id becomes a directory name, so containment is a property of the id itself rather than of a path check after the fact — `../escape`, `a/b`, and an absolute path are all rejected as ids.
- **An id that is already taken.** A copy never overwrites: any root supplying the id refuses it (a user directory named like a shipped preset would be shadowed by it), and a directory occupying the name on disk refuses it too. Discovery lists such a directory as a broken preset, so the refusal's way out — delete it — is on the same page that reported it.
- **An unknown source.** The source may be any trust — copying a shipped preset is the primary case — but it must exist; a failed copy rolls its half-made directory back rather than leaving one discovery cannot see.

The copied tree is re-tightened to owner-only (`0o600` files keeping their owner-execute bit, `0o700` directories), symlinks are dereferenced so the copy is self-contained, and the root is created on first copy — a deployment configuring a user root that does not exist yet is the normal first-run state. The copied `preset.yml` is rewritten: the source's description is kept for the author to edit in place, but its name and roster `order` are dropped — a copy presenting itself identically to its source, or sorted into the shipped set's declared order, would make the roster stop distinguishing them. `remove()` refuses a preset that ships with the deployment; the shipped set is the known-good compositions copies start from.

### How a preset's rows resolve

A row's **package name** resolves from the host composition, not from the preset directory. The Loader normally resolves an entry against its own tree's `baseUrl`, which for a preset is wherever the composition file sits; a locally authored preset lives under the user's home, where Node's upward `node_modules` walk never reaches the harness, so every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` row would fail to import. The mount records the host base before plugging the subtree and sends bare specifiers there.

A **relative** path still resolves from the preset's own directory, so a preset's own plugin files and skill directories travel with it.

An **absolute** filesystem path keeps its own location. The mount converts it to a `file:` URL before ESM import so POSIX paths and Windows drive-letter or UNC paths use a specifier Node accepts.

### Display metadata and the declared role

A preset may publish display text and one authority claim in an optional `preset.yml` beside its composition:

```yaml
name: 极简模式
description: 仅提供持久 bash 与 str_replace_editor 的双工具编码 Agent。
role: implementer
```

# The candidate arm's composition: the fixture's three craft skills as a second
# skill root, registered in this preset's scope layer so only the cells joined
# to it see the catalog. The skills carry generic practice for a checked
# command-line program (channel discipline, reading a specification for its
# corners, working against a node:test suite inside a budget) and no
# task-specific content.
#
# `includeDefaultRoots: false` and a provider name of its own keep this root
# beside the base composition's `filesystem` provider rather than shadowing it:
# the two presets differ in this catalog and in nothing else. The root is found
# from the repository root above `baseUrl`, which inside a preset tree is the
# preset's own directory.
- name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
  config:
    providerName: craft
    includeDefaultRoots: false
    watch: false
    customSkillDirs:
      - !!js |
          (() => {
            const { fileURLToPath } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:url')
            const { existsSync } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs')
            const { dirname, join } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path')
            let dir = fileURLToPath(baseUrl)
            while (!existsSync(join(dir, 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'))) {
              const parent = dirname(dir)
              if (parent === dir) throw new Error('bench-craft preset: repository root not found above ' + baseUrl)
              dir = parent
            }
            return join(dir, 'examples', 'headless-agent', 'tests', 'fixtures', 'proving-ground-bench', 'skills')

# @deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The read barrier (`ctx.readBarrier`): the policy home for reads an `implementer` or `judge` session must not perform, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. It owns one validator-owned directory tree, mints the per-run directory a validator stocks with what its checks execute, collects the directories other plugins register, resolves one policy per session, decides containment through the filesystem seam, records what each session composed, and verifies the host attestation a `host` isolation claim needs. It denies nothing by itself: each path-opening capability enforces the decision in the operation that opens paths, which is what [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`](../../fs/fs-read-barrier/README.md) does for `ctx.fs`. The [read-barrier Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-read-barrier.md) owns the design rationale.

## Config

```yaml
- id: read-barrier
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
  config:
    root: ~/.dsh/verification
    denyRoots:
      - /srv/evaluation/fixtures
    hostAttestation: /srv/attestation/run.json
    isolationClaim: process
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `root` (default `<harness home>/verification`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns. Created `0700` at load; an existing directory readable beyond its owner is rejected there, and so is a path that is not absolute after `~` expansion. |
| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Further absolute or `~`-prefixed directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
| `hostAttestation` (default none) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed file an external account writes. Without a file the barrier verified, no certificate may claim `host` isolation. |
| `isolationClaim` (default `none`) | The isolation this deployment intends its certificates to claim: `none`, `process`, or `host`. It decides only what a capability the harness cannot fence in-process does for an implementer session — refuse to start under `process` or `host`, run unenforced under `none`. It grants nothing; what a certificate may actually claim is decided by [`dsh-verification`](../verification/README.md) over the census below. |

The denied set for a role is deliberately not a field, and neither are the authorities a role may hold: both are security invariants, not deployment choices. The service requires `fs`, because containment is decided through that seam rather than by parsing path strings.

## Service contract

`ctx.readBarrier.reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` owner-only, records that session as the `implementer`, and returns the absolute path; reserving the same session again returns the same directory. It is synchronous so the role is in force the moment the caller returns. A validator writes there what its checks execute — the standard snapshot, one script per check, any held-out fixture — so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. The reservation is dropped when the agent is disposed.

`ctx.readBarrier.reservation(agent)` reads back the directory a session already holds, without minting one. Every consumer that only needs to find a reservation asks here — the [instrument](../tool-standard-author/README.md) locating the reference program it samples, for one: reserving is what makes an unmarked session the implementer, so a reader that reserved to find out would demote the session it was reading for.

`ctx.readBarrier.protect(path)` denies one more directory for as long as the registration lives and returns its disposer, so a plugin that owns a directory contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration. Two registrations of one path both hold; the directory leaves the denied set when the last is disposed.

`ctx.readBarrier.denyFor(session, path)` denies one directory to ONE session for as long as the registration lives and returns its disposer. It is the per-session sibling of `protect()`, for a directory a caller owns only while one run lasts: the [environment runner](../../improvement/environment-runner/README.md) denies each cell the directory its workspace sits in, which every sibling cell and the runner's own session keep reading. Two registrations of one path for one session both hold.

`ctx.readBarrier.enforce(capability)` records that one path-opening capability — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, or `workflow` — denies the barrier's directories in the operation that opens paths, for as long as the registration lives, and returns its disposer. A composed capability without one is `unenforced` in the census, and an isolation claim above `none` is refused while any such entry stands. [`enforceReadBarrier`](../../sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) is how each sandbox-consuming executor makes this call, so no capability claims an enforcement its own backend never applies.

`ctx.readBarrier.enforceByRefusal(capability)` is its sibling for the executors this process cannot fence: a worker thread recovers the host process's privileges and an out-of-process agent brings its own tool stack, so neither can deny a read where it opens paths. The census follows `isolationClaim` — `denied-at-executor` under `process` or `host`, where `startRefusal` refuses every implementer start, and `unenforced` with that reason under `none`, where the capability runs and denies nothing.

`ctx.readBarrier.cannotEnforce(capability, reason)` records that a composed capability cannot enforce on this host, with the reason the capability supplies — the backend that cannot express the denial, or a deployment mode that runs commands unconfined. The certificate refused over such a census names the reason instead of only the capability. An `enforce()` registration for the same capability outranks it.

`ctx.readBarrier.startRefusal(capability, session)` answers the exact refusal a capability that cannot be confined in-process must return instead of starting, or `undefined` when it may start. Every start of such a capability asks here, so the refusal is decided in the operation that would open the paths. `startRefusalMessage(capability, claim)` owns the text.

`deniedReadRoots(policy)` answers the directories a resolved policy actually denies its holder: every denied directory for a role in `DENIED_ROLES` — `implementer` and `judge` — and none for any other. One place decides which roles the denied set binds, so a process runner filling its own denial and the in-process `denies()` test cannot disagree. `grantedReadRoot(policy)` is its companion for the granted workspace, answering it under the same rule and `undefined` for every other role.

**A denied ancestor never removes the session's own workspace.** A policy carries `granted` — the session's cwd — beside `denied`, and the two are ordered: a denied directory that is a STRICT ancestor of the workspace denies the rest of that ancestor's subtree and leaves the workspace whole; a denied directory that IS the workspace, or that lies inside it, denies exactly as it would without the grant. Every enforcing capability expresses that same order in its own dialect, so a cell denied the run directory it sits in still reads and writes its own files.

`ctx.readBarrier.declareComposition(agent, { presetId, role })` records what a preset roster composed for one agent. A declared role outranks a reservation, because only the composition knows what was actually mounted; a preset that declares none leaves the reservation to decide. [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../preset/agent-presets/README.md) is the only caller: nothing a session itself runs may raise its own role.

`ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied, granted? }`. A session whose preset declared a role holds that role; otherwise a session holding a reservation is the `implementer`, and every other session and every agentless call is `unrestricted`. `denied` lists the root first, then the configured extras, then each `protect()` registration, then each `denyFor()` registration for this session, without repeats. `granted` is the session's own cwd, absent for a session created without one and for an agentless call.

`ctx.readBarrier.denies(policy, target)` decides containment for an already-resolved `FsTarget`. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing. For an `implementer` or a `judge`, each denied directory is canonicalized through `ctx.fs.resolve` immediately before `ctx.fs.contains` tests it, so an ancestor symlink swapped since the target was resolved is caught; a directory the backend cannot resolve leaves containment undecidable and the read is denied. The granted workspace is resolved the same way and carves out only the denials above it; a grant the backend cannot resolve carves nothing, so the denial holds.

The two denied roles are denied the same set for different reasons. An `implementer` must not read the standard it is measured against; a `judge` must not read it either, because the check instructions behind the evidence it was handed are exactly what a blind audit withholds — [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-judge`](../judge/README.md) owns that arrangement.

`ctx.readBarrier.recordDenial(session, policy, capability, target)` appends the log-only `read-barrier/denied` event — `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, with `capability` naming the seam that refused — and returns the payload it appended. The barrier owns the write so every refusing seam produces the same evidence; the path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the record adds evidence and no new disclosure.

The declared authorities are `session-log`, `plugin-mount`, `runtime-introspection`, and `standard-author` — the last one carried by the tool that runs a recreation task's reference program and writes the standard's case bodies. `deniedAuthority(role, authority)` answers the first authority a role may not hold. Every authority a [`ToolDefinition`](../../core/tools/README.md) declares is denied to a role in `DENIED_ROLES` and none to any other, so an authority merged into `ToolAuthorityMap` later is denied by this same rule rather than by a list that would go stale. `authorityDenialMessage(tool, authority, role)` owns the text the guard returns, naming the role it refused.

### The composition census

Before a session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` carrying `{ version, role, presetId?, root, denied, granted?, census, enforcement }`. `granted` is the workspace the denied set is ordered around: without it a census that denies an ancestor of the workspace would read as denying the workspace too. `census` is one `{ name, authority }` entry per tool the session's registry view resolves, sorted by tool name because registry order follows concurrent Loader mounts and would otherwise make two runs of one composition record different censuses; it makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability, valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`, in a fixed capability order; an `unenforced` entry carries the `reason` its capability recorded, when it recorded one. When a `hostAttestation` file is configured and verifies — a regular file owned by another operating-system account and unwritable by this one — the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/attestation` beside it, carrying `{ version, path, owner, sha256 }`. An absent or unverifiable file records nothing and logs a warning; the claim it would have supported is refused instead of the run failing.

The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` on each agent's own context at `agent/created`, denying any execution whose definition carries an authority that session's role forbids. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission. The `mountPreset` audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards.

The separately published `./invariant` companion rejects a refusal recorded for any role the barrier denies nothing, one carrying an unknown payload version or capability, and one naming a different barrier root than the session's earlier records. It rejects a census of unknown version, one for an unknown role, one recording enforcement for a capability that opens no path or a decision outside the vocabulary, and a second census in one session; and an attestation of unknown version or with no file path.
